CONFIRM C0001 — `evaluate_fix()` runs `test_cmd` unchanged in `cwd=tmpdir`, so absolute paths or repo-relative test targets in the command still point at real files outside the sandbox. That violates the module’s stated “sandboxed (tempdir, never modifies actual source)” contract and can produce false SAFE/HARMFUL verdicts against unpatched code.

CONFIRM C0002 — pre/post comparison is not like-for-like. Baselines are collected on `target_path` in the live tree, while post-fix counts are collected on `patched_path` inside the temp tree. For pyright/mypy/ruff/bandit, import resolution and config discovery depend on analysis root, so the delta is mechanically unsound.

CONFIRM C0007 — same root cause as C0002/C0026/C0018. The issue is not just “original vs sandbox”; it is “single live file vs mirrored project fragment”, which changes tool behavior materially.

CONFIRM C0008 — `_count_tool_issues()` converts tool execution failure into `0`, which makes downstream verdict logic treat “tool unavailable/crashed/timed out” as “no issues found”. That can mark unevaluable fixes as SAFE/NEUTRAL silently.

CONFIRM C0009 — `_run_tool()` returns `stderr="TIMEOUT"` on timeout, but `run_pyright()` only special-cases `"NOT_FOUND"` and otherwise attempts JSON parse, logs warning, then returns `[]`. Timeout therefore degrades to “zero diagnostics”, contaminating both health scan and fix evaluation.

CONFIRM C0010 — the module docstring and public API claim four capabilities, including “Defect detect — classify findings by defect category”, but there is no public entry point for this capability beyond per-tool categorisation during scan. The feature is not exposed as an independently callable function as documented.

CONFIRM C0012 — early return on `not existing` yields `HealthScan(elapsed_s=...)` with empty `tools_available`, so consumers cannot distinguish “no files” from “field omitted/unknown”. That is an interface defect in a structured report object.

CONFIRM C0013 — `_find_target_file()` falling back to `source_paths[0]` when no path is resolved can evaluate and report on the wrong file. In fix evaluation this is silently wrong, not merely approximate.

CONFIRM C0025 — suffix match uses `sp_path.endswith(os.sep + match)`. If `match` contains `/` while running on Windows, or `sp_path` and match differ in separator style, a valid described path is missed and the function falls through to the unsafe fallback. Normalization is required.

CONFIRM C0026 — baseline tool counts are run against the live `target_path`, not the sandbox copy. That breaks the “never modifies actual source” / sandbox comparison semantics even when no tests are run.

CONFIRM C0027 — same evidence as C0008. Returning `0` on exception is specifically dangerous because `_compute_fix_verdict()` interprets non-positive net change as acceptable.

CONFIRM C0034 — `_create_sandbox()` copies only `source_paths` plus the patched target. If the file under test imports other project modules not included in `source_paths`, pyright/mypy/test execution in the sandbox sees missing modules and produces artifacts unrelated to the patch. This can make fix evaluation never fire cleanly for realistic multi-file changes.

CONFIRM C0035 — `_apply_fix_to_source()` Strategy 2 accepts any 5+ line syntactically valid Python block as a whole-file replacement. A proposed fix containing only a helper function or code sample can replace the entire file, making the evaluator test nonsense rather than the intended patch.

CONFIRM C0037 — sequential application of multi-line range replacements mutates line indices for later matches. A second `Lines N-M` edit can target the wrong region after an earlier range changed line structure.

EXTEND C0034 | Consequence reaches health of the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature: because imports outside `source_paths` are omitted, `evaluate_fix()` can systematically classify valid fixes as HARMFUL due to sandbox-induced import failures, so the key new capability does not work end-to-end on ordinary project files with transitive local imports.

EXTEND C0008 | This also corrupts `scan_health()` indirectly where tool runners degrade timeout/parse failure to empty diagnostics. The system then emits “healthy” reports when tools were non-functional, misleading pacing and downstream review.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_mypy()` cannot parse standard mypy diagnostics that omit a column number. The regex requires `file:line:col: severity: ...`, but mypy commonly emits `file.py:123: error: ...` unless column reporting is consistently present for that message. In this function, any non-matching line is silently dropped, so the health scan and fix evaluator undercount or fully miss mypy findings. Evidence: the parser pattern is `^(.+?):(\d+):(\d+):\s+(error|warning|note):...$`, which makes the column mandatory.
FOLLOW: Mypy is one of four advertised health-scan tools. If its output is partially or wholly discarded, `scan_health()` produces silently wrong totals and category counts, and `evaluate_fix()` can mark patches SAFE/NEUTRAL despite new mypy errors. This is HIGH in a PoC because the feature appears to run but yields misleading results.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Make the column group optional in the regex and default `column` to 0 when absent, e.g. accept both `file:line: error:` and `file:line:col: error:` formats.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` advertises comparison of “type checkers and linters” before/after, and the module-level health scan includes mypy, but fix evaluation never runs mypy at all. It only records pyright/ruff/bandit pre/post counts (`pre_type_errors`/`new_type_errors` come solely from `run_pyright`). Evidence: `evaluate_fix()` calls `_count_tool_issues(run_pyright, ...)`, `_count_tool_issues(run_ruff, ...)`, `_count_tool_issues(run_bandit, ...)`; `run_mypy()` is unused in fix evaluation and there are no mypy fields in `FixEvaluation`.
FOLLOW: The endocrine layer can report a proposed fix SAFE even when it introduces mypy-only type regressions. That is silently wrong relative to the documented capability and inconsistent with `scan_health()`, which does run mypy. The gap is material because users will assume “type checkers” plural were applied.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Include mypy in pre/post fix evaluation and verdict computation by adding mypy issue counts to `FixEvaluation` and treating newly introduced mypy errors the same way as pyright regressions.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_create_sandbox()` can return a sandbox with no copy of the target file’s original package metadata files (`__init__.py`) when those files are not explicitly listed in `source_paths`. The function claims to preserve package structure, but it only copies listed files. Evidence: the copy loop iterates only `for src in source_paths`, then optionally writes `target_path`; no ancestor package files are copied.
FOLLOW: Even if sibling modules are present in `source_paths`, missing `__init__.py` files can change import resolution for tests and static analyzers inside the sandbox, causing false failures or different module identities than the live tree. This is a direct end-to-end defect in sandbox fidelity.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — When building the sandbox tree, also copy `__init__.py` files along the relative path from the common ancestor to each copied Python file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.34
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` can emit a false `slow_model` signal for a single model run. With one timing entry, `median_duration` equals that model’s duration, making the relative threshold impossible (`rt.duration_s > median*2.5`), so slow-model detection is effectively dead for one model; with two models, using upper-middle median further weakens detection. Evidence: the function only compares against within-round median and has no minimum-sample guard or absolute fallback.
FOLLOW: The advertised pacing feature “timing ... monitoring” does not fire meaningfully on small model sets or degraded runs where only one or two models respond. That weakens the insect brain’s ability to react to slowdown exactly when failures reduce the population.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Require at least 3 timing samples for relative slow-model detection; otherwise skip emitting `slow_model` rather than implying the feature is operating.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_pyright()` records pyright `severity` verbatim, but downstream aggregation expects normalized buckets shared with other tools. Pyright JSON commonly uses `"error"`, `"warning"`, and `"information"`, while the module docstrings and `ToolDiagnostic.severity` comment specify `"error", "warning", "info"`. Evidence: `severity_raw = diag.get("severity", "error")` is stored unchanged; no mapping from `"information"` to `"info"` exists.
FOLLOW: `counts_by_severity` becomes inconsistent across tools (`info` for bandit low, `information` for pyright info), so consumers reading aggregate severity totals receive split buckets for the same concept. This silently distorts health metrics and any thresholding built on them.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Normalize pyright severities on ingest, mapping `"information"` to `"info"` and passing through `"error"`/`"warning"`.
VERIFIED: TRUE
